messages:
incident-bot: [P1] Dedicated pool 'pegasus-prod' - GPU util 98%, queue depth rising. Triggered 2024-05-12 03:24:36 UTC. Pager: pd://P-12345. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/pegasus-dedicated-capacity. @oncall please acknowledge.

amanda_oncall: ack — investigating now. Pulling metrics and pool state.

josh_sre: quick snapshot: 95th latency jumped from ~120ms -> 1.8s since ~03:18. queue_length=420, inflight=4k tokens. Pool config shows min_size=4 max_size=4 (single-tenant). No autoscale webhook triggered because pool is at max.

lia_pegasus_sre: Confirming — Pegasus infra team rolled a nightly export at 03:15 that hit production model endpoints (not isolated). We're seeing sustained inference-heavy traffic. Can pause the job if needed.

amanda_oncall: Options: 1) approve burst attach (+2 GPUs) from burst reserve, 2) ask Pegasus to throttle/pause, 3) temporary fallback to lighter model variant. Which first? @infra-ops @product-sre

infra-ops: burst-reserve has 2xA100 available in us-west-2, warm. Attach time ~6m. NOTE: this tenant has a manual-burst approval policy (enterprise billing guardrail) — requires oncall+cust approval or ops override.

product-sre: recommend dual approach: enable burst to immediately relieve tail latencies, and ask Pegasus to pause the nightly export while we assess. Also apply a rate-limit rule on non-critical routes (/batch/*) to throttle background load.

amanda_oncall: I'll request customer pause now. Pinging Pegasus contact via their workspace: @lia_pegasus_sre has notified them. Starting burst attach command: 
```
rictl pools attach-burst --pool pegasus-prod --count 2 --source burst-pool-2 --reason "emergency - queue saturation"
```

amanda_oncall: executing... attaching 2 GPUs -> attaching.

infra-ops: approving override from infra to attach (cost center verified).

amanda_oncall: attach complete. Pool size now 6 GPUs. Metrics: queue_length down from 420 -> 80 in ~4m. 95th latency dropped to ~300ms and trending down. :thumbsup:

lia_pegasus_sre: Pegasus engineering confirms they paused the nightly export at 03:30 UTC. They're following up with a mitigation plan (throttle+split job). They asked for a short window to validate before we detach burst.

josh_sre: logs show no GPU OOMs, just scheduling contention. Good candidate for changing autoscale policy: raise max_size or convert burst to permanent for this tenant if they expect sustained load. Need commercial approval for capacity commit.

product-sre: capture next steps: (1) short postmortem with timeline and cost estimate for burst (2) update autoscale policy or set min_size to 6 if Pegasus wants continuous capacity (3) implement route-based rate limits for batch endpoints and onboarding docs for tenant-run batch jobs.

amanda_oncall: Handoff: I'm handing incident to night oncall @ben_night at 04:00 UTC. Ben, please monitor queue_length and 95th latency. Escalate if queue > 200 or 95th > 1s for 5m.

ben_night: ack. Monitoring dashboard pinned. Will rollback burst after 2 hours if Pegasus confirms stable or detach earlier if safe.

josh_sre: adding runbook note: when single-tenant pool hits max_size and queue>200, recommend immediate burst attach + customer pause. File follow-up ticket: INF-3421 (pegasus postmortem & policy changes).

amanda_oncall: Closing paging — incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Leaving this thread open for postmortem items.

incident-bot: Incident state updated: MITIGATED. Pager cleared at 2024-05-12 03:44:00 UTC. Reminder: schedule postmortem and include billing impact for burst attach (~2 A100-hours).
